notes: Drama and gossip. 'reasons' are why two friends fall out ({a_first}, {b_first}). 'open' starts a gossip text from a friend. Each scene's choices run a drama op (drama.py does what it says); 'say' lines are what happens, by outcome.
reasons: a screenshot from the group chat
who got invited to a party and who didn't
a bet over a game that got way too serious
a borrowed hoodie that never came back
open: ok you can't say anything but

sides.title: {a_first} vs. {b_first}
text: {a_first} and {b_first} aren't speaking. It started with {reason}, and now both of them keep looking at you like you have to pick.
It's a whole thing: {a_first} and {b_first} blew up over {reason}. Each of them has texted you their side. Twice.

choices.label: Get them in a room together.

partner.title: {other_first}
text: People keep saying {other_first} is into {partner_first}. And {partner_first} doesn't exactly seem to hate it.
Third time this week you've seen {partner_first} laughing with {other_first}. Your friends have noticed too.

crush_taken.title: {crush_first} and {other_first}
text: {crush_first} and {other_first} are officially a thing. It's all anyone's talking about. Great.
You find out the way everyone does: {crush_first} and {other_first}, holding hands by the lockers.

fallout.title: {them_first}
text: {them_first} hasn't said a word to you since {reason}. You used to talk every day.
{them_first} walks right past you in the hall. Ever since {reason}, it's been like this.

makeup.title: {them_first} wants to talk
text: {them_first} texted: "hey. can we talk? i miss this."
{them_first} catches you after class. "Can we just... fix this?"

side_a: {a_first} is so relieved. {b_first} sees you two together at lunch and walks the other way.
side_b: {b_first} is so relieved. {a_first} sees you two together at lunch and walks the other way.
stay_out: Neither of them is thrilled, but neither of them is mad at you either. Mostly.
mediate_ok: It's awkward for ten minutes. Then {a_first} laughs at something {b_first} says, and it's over. You did that.
mediate_bad: It goes worse than before. Now they're both a little annoyed with you too.
ask_partner_ok: "Seriously? It's nothing. It's you." {partner_first} means it. You can tell.
ask_partner_bad: {partner_first} gets defensive, fast. Too fast. Things are quiet between you for a while.
warn_other_ok: {other_first} gets the message. {partner_first} thinks it's kind of cute, actually.
warn_other_bad: {other_first} laughs it off. {partner_first} is embarrassed you did that.
let_go_ok: You let it go. A week later it's nothing, like it always was.
let_go_bad: You let it go. You'll hear about it later, though.
happy_for: It stings. You say congrats anyway, and {crush_first} looks like they really appreciate it.
confess_ok: {crush_first} goes quiet for a long time. Then: "I think I've been with the wrong person." By Friday, everything's different.
confess_bad: {crush_first} looks at you like you've lost your mind. "I'm with {other_first}. You know that." It gets around.
move_on: You mute {crush_first}'s stories. It helps more than you thought it would.
apologize_ok: {them_first} hears you out. "Yeah. Me too." Just like that, you're good.
apologize_bad: "Okay," {them_first} says, and walks away. Not yet, apparently.
give_time: You leave it alone. Maybe they'll come around.
write_off: Fine. Their loss. You stop looking for them in the hallway.
hear_out: You talk for an hour. It's like nothing ever happened. Okay, almost.
leave_it: You leave it on read. Some things don't need fixing.
